summary: The root شقق primarily means to cleave, split, or tear something apart, creating a fissure or division. It can also imply difficulty or hardship, as if something is being split open with effort.

headwords.def: شَاقٌّ Difficult, hard, distressing, grievous, afflicting, troubling, molesting, fatiguing, or wearying. (KL.) One says أَمْرٌ شَاقٌّ [ An affair, or event, that is difficult, &c.]; from شَقَّ عَلَيْنَا الأَمْرُ . (Msb.) And شُقَّةٌ شَاقَّةٌ (S, Msb) A long journey [ that is difficult, &c.]. (Msb.)
